title: Rain on One Side of the Mountain

sentences.text: When wind carries moist air toward a mountain, the air has to rise.
Rising air cools. Cool air cannot hold as much invisible water vapor as warm air can.
Tiny droplets form, clouds grow, and rain or snow falls on the side where the air is climbing.
That wet side is called the windward side, because it faces the oncoming wind.
After the air crosses the peak, it sinks down the other side.
Sinking air warms, and warmer air can hold more vapor, so the clouds often thin out.
The side sheltered from the wind is called the leeward side.
It sits in a rain shadow, a drier region on the far side of a mountain.
The same storm can water a forest on one slope and leave the other slope brown.
A rain shadow does not mean the leeward side never gets rain. It usually gets less.
Oceans, seasons, and the height of the mountain all change how strong the shadow is.
A very tall mountain range can block a great deal of moisture.
People who farm or plan towns pay attention, because rivers, crops, and wildfire risk can differ on the two sides.
If you ride from a green slope into a dry valley in a single hour, a rain shadow may explain the change.
The mountain did not drink the water. It forced the air to drop much of that water on the way up.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How to move a mountain closer to the ocean
Why snow never falls on any slope
How valleys drink water through their roots
Why one side of a mountain is often wetter than the other

questions.explanation: The passage explains rising, cooling air on the windward side and drier air on the leeward side. That difference is the main idea.

questions.prompt: In this passage, the leeward side is which side?

choices.text: The side sheltered from the wind, often in the rain shadow
The side the wind hits first
The bottom of the ocean
The inside of a raindrop

questions.explanation: The passage says the leeward side is sheltered from the wind and sits in the drier rain shadow. The windward side is the one facing the wind.

questions.prompt: What happens to air as it rises up the mountain?

choices.text: It always gets warmer
It cools
It turns into solid rock
It stops moving at the foot of the slope

questions.explanation: The passage says rising air cools, and cool air cannot hold as much water vapor. That cooling comes before the rain.

questions.prompt: A town on the leeward side wants gardens that need a lot of rain. What should the town figure out?

choices.text: The gardens will be soaked every day by the rain shadow
Windward and leeward receive exactly the same rain
Those gardens may need extra water because that side is usually drier
Mountains stop all wind, so no water can evaporate

questions.explanation: The passage says the leeward side usually gets less rain, not none. A garden that needs a lot of water would likely need help beyond the local rainfall.

choices.text: Air sinks first, then rises, then the ocean moves
Rain falls, then the air rises, then clouds disappear forever
The leeward side gets rain before the windward side
Air rises and cools, rain falls, then air sinks and warms

questions.explanation: Moist air rises and cools first, which brings rain on the climbing side. After the peak, the air sinks and warms. That is the order the passage describes.
